hero.heading: Insects Limited, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built September 27, 2026, from insectslimited.com and its store, and from the company's own published research summary. No federal data is used, and this page says why. Every number is labeled; the assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: Exact computed endpoints: $20,500.00 and $88,000.00, rounded to the nearest $5,000 for display.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Dollars of product you ship in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per million dollars shipped.

presets.label: Our catalog prices passed every cost through

model.disclosure: This model contains no federal number. We checked the chemical price indexes and none maps truthfully onto pheromone synthesis; the industrial chemicals index has barely moved this year. Every figure on this page is our assumption, printed to be corrected.

terms.label: The price of free expert hours

model.formulaText: Moved per $1,000,000 shipped = expert hours × loaded rate + 1,000,000 × absorbed cents per dollar
model.plainText: In words, what the free expert hours cost at their loaded rate, plus the slice of every product dollar that cost creep ate while catalog prices stood.
model.callout: Your experts answer the world's pest questions at no charge. Those hours are your differentiator, and they ship at a price of zero. Nobody knows what they cost per million dollars sold, or which of your four audiences earns the hours it consumes. Those numbers exist in your records, unread.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: You still publish the sentence this company was founded on in 1981: the future of pest control is without the use of toxic chemicals [[OBSERVED]].
You invite anyone to send a pest question to a board certified entomologist, at no charge, and your identifications are free [[OBSERVED]].
Your guides are free, and your store posts its prices in the open [[OBSERVED]].
You name your four audiences plainly: food safety, homes, museums, and pest management professionals [[OBSERVED]].

Your own recent post about a product you discontinued says, in your words, that technically it worked and commercially it did not; a USDA and Kansas State study later measured it at 95.8 percent accuracy [[OBSERVED]].
